title: Mara and the Alibi
premise: Insurance investigator Casper Sterling receives two letters about the decade-old Harrow Bay drowning: one confessing to the murder of local matriarch Vivian Ashcombe, the other promising a second confession if he attends the reopening of the case. As Casper's photographic memory dredges up details from the original file that never fit, he discovers the town's leading families built their fortunes on a falsified alibi — and that his own late mother was the investigator who buried it. Racing a trial date and an antagonist who knows exactly which memories to weaponize against him, Casper must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the only person who ever made him feel he belonged. In the end, the second confession arrives from the least likely writer: Vivian herself, alive, having staged her death to test who would protect the lie.
about_author: Kestrel Sterling is the pen name of a former coastal claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters for a living before turning to fiction. They write mysteries from a houseboat office, insisting that every alibi they've ever audited taught them something about how stories are built to be believed.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Handwriting
chapters.summary: Casper Sterling, closing another routine fraud case, receives twin letters about the ten-year-old Harrow Bay drowning of Vivian Ashcombe: a full confession, unsigned, and a second note promising 'the rest' if he comes in person. His photographic memory flags that both letters share the same pen pressure. POV: Casper. Beat: cold curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: The File That Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: Casper pulls the archived Ashcombe claim and finds pages cleanly excised — including the original alibi statement from Vivian's business partner, Daniel Voss. Someone with institutional access sanitized it. He requests the trial transcript under a pretext. POV: Casper. Beat: the first vertigo of realizing the record itself has been edited.

chapters.title: Harrow Bay Welcomes You
chapters.summary: Casper arrives in the fog-bound town where everyone smiles a beat too long. At the marina inn, the owner recognizes his surname and flinches. A teenage girl, Nell Okafor, watches him from the pier and leaves a note: 'You're the second one to ask about the water.' POV: Casper. Beat: belonging offered and withheld in the same handshake.

chapters.title: The Confessor Who Cried
chapters.summary: Casper tracks the confessed letter to Ruth Ashcombe, Vivian's estranged daughter, now a hospice nurse dying of the same illness that killed her mother. Ruth admits she wrote a confession — but insists she wrote three, mailed to three investigators, as a test. Only Casper came. POV: Casper. Beat: pity tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Nell leads Casper to the cove where Vivian drowned; her grandmother was the last witness questioned. The tide chart from the night of the death contradicts the official timeline by forty minutes — a discrepancy Casper's memory confirms was in the excised pages. POV: Nell. Beat: the thrill of being believed by an adult for the first time.

chapters.title: Daniel Voss, Pillar of the Community
chapters.summary: Voss, now running the family cannery empire, hosts Casper with practiced charm and offers him a consulting retainer to 'advise on risk.' The bribe is elegant, deniable, and unmistakable. Casper declines; Voss's smile doesn't move. POV: Casper. Beat: power revealing its manners.

chapters.title: My Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Casper finds the excised alibi page — and recognizes the certification signature: his own mother, the investigator who worked the original case before leaving town and never speaking of it. The letter-writer knew. That was the hook. POV: Casper. Beat: identity cracking open like a hull.

chapters.title: Three Letters, Three Investigators
chapters.summary: Casper locates the second recipient: a retired detective, Albrecht, living drunk and afraid two counties over. Albrecht took Voss's money in year one and has been paid annually since. He warns Casper: 'They don't threaten you. They make you useful.' POV: Albrecht. Beat: corruption shown as maintenance, not event.

chapters.title: The Trial Date
chapters.summary: A judge grants a motion to reopen based on an anonymous filing — someone wants this public, fast. The trial is set for six weeks out. Casper realizes the letters weren't a confession at all; they were a summons timed to force the case open before evidence rots further. POV: Casper. Beat: the trap's shape becoming visible.

chapters.title: Nell's Grandmother Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Casper interviews the elderly witness, whose account shifts subtly each telling — until he realizes she's reciting a rehearsed version, terrified of getting it 'right' incorrectly. Her true memory surfaces in fragments: a second boat, engine idling. POV: alternating Casper and the grandmother. Beat: memory as contested territory.

chapters.title: Useful
chapters.summary: Someone leaks Casper's mother's old personnel file — a fabricated disciplinary history — to discredit anything he finds. Local paper runs it. Casper's professional reputation, his one source of belonging, begins dissolving publicly. POV: Casper. Beat: isolation engineered with precision.

chapters.title: Ruth's Third Letter
chapters.summary: Ruth, weakening fast, gives Casper the third letter unopened: instructions she was paid to mail but never did. Inside is a photograph of the cove taken after the drowning — showing Voss's boat, and a figure on the dock wearing his mother's coat. POV: Casper. Beat: dread arriving as recognition.

chapters.title: The Coat
chapters.summary: Casper reconstructs the night: his mother didn't just certify the false alibi — she was there, and the photo proves Voss used her presence as leverage ever after. She didn't leave town; she was exiled with the truth in her pocket. POV: Casper, interleaved with reconstructed memory. Beat: grief reorganizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore
chapters.summary: Casper maps the web: the coroner, the harbor master, two council members — all pensioned, promoted, or silenced by Voss over a decade. The alibi wasn't one lie; it was an economy. POV: Casper. Beat: power and its corruption rendered as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: A Visit at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Casper's boat trailer is sabotaged; then his room is searched, professionally. Nell is followed home. Casper understands he's no longer investigating — he's being managed. He sends copies of everything to three separate lawyers. POV: Nell. Beat: fear without the option of retreat.

chapters.title: Albrecht Comes Clean
chapters.summary: Shamed by Casper's refusal to be bought, Albrecht surrenders his payment ledger — ten years of dates and amounts — and names the intermediary: Voss's lawyer, who also happens to represent the estate. The ledger corroborates the tide discrepancy exactly. POV: Albrecht. Beat: a small redemption purchased too late to be clean.

chapters.title: The Second Promise
chapters.summary: A new letter arrives, matching the originals: 'The rest, as promised. Come alone to the cove the night before trial.' Casper recognizes the handwriting pressure instantly — it matches Ruth's hospice charts, but the phrasing is someone else's. Ruth is dictating. POV: Casper. Beat: the puppeteer's hand finally twitching into view.

chapters.title: Pretrial
chapters.summary: At the motions hearing, Voss's counsel moves to exclude the ledger and the photograph. The grandmother, subpoenaed, recants on the stand — then, seeing Nell in the gallery, stops mid-sentence and tells the truth instead. The courtroom detonates quietly. POV: Casper. Beat: courage as contagion.

chapters.title: The Cove, Night Before
chapters.summary: Casper goes to the cove alone — but not unarmed: Nell records from the bluff, and a deputy he trusts waits offshore. Voss appears and confesses plainly, certain nothing can touch him, explaining how he turned Casper's mother's presence into a decade of silence. Then he offers Casper the same trade. POV: Casper. Beat: the climax of temptation.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: Vivian Ashcombe steps out of the dark, alive — her drowning staged with Voss's help to escape his control, her 'death' the leverage that kept the town complicit. She sent the letters to force the truth out on her terms, using Casper because his mother once showed her kindness. POV: Vivian. Beat: identity revealed as the final misdirection.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: Vivian surrenders; Voss, recorded and ledgered, is arrested as the trial opens and collapses within a week. The grandmother's testimony stands. Casper files the report his mother never could, signing both their names. Ruth dies knowing the record reads true. POV: Casper. Beat: justice as repair, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: Belonging, Provisionally
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Casper stays in Harrow Bay through the settlement of the estate claims. Nell asks if he'll take her on as an apprentice in observation. He says yes — the first case he takes that no one asked him to close. POV: Casper. Beat: belonging chosen rather than granted.
